title: Two-Axis Token Valuation Experiment + Enterprise SQ Contract Alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: evaluate a two-axis pricing experiment for Hosted API that separates token valuation along ingress (input) and egress (output/streaming) dimensions, and validate the commercial and legal implications for enterprise contract language and Security Questionnaires (SQs). The experiment aims to find a billing configuration that better aligns cost-to-serve with customer value for streaming-heavy workloads while keeping friction low for PLG adoption. We will model several asymmetric rate pairs (e.g., 0.6x ingress : 1.4x egress), a soft streaming floor with a grace-credit window, and enterprise commit variants that translate expected monthly usage into dollar commits and minimums. The scope includes telemetry instrumentation, billing simulation, contract template clauses for committed minimums + grace credits, and a checklist for SQ answers that reflect any policy changes (data residency, buffering/retention, and audit trail for metering).
hypotheses: H1: Charging higher for output tokens than input will reduce cost leakage for streaming-first applications without materially reducing adoption across developer sign-ups.
H2: A small streaming floor with a 72-hour grace-credit window reduces churn from bursty customers compared to a hard minimum while preserving revenue predictability for enterprise commits.
H3: Clear SQ responses and explicit contract language about metering and burst credits will shorten legal negotiation cycles for mid-market deals.
metrics: Primary: net revenue per active API customer over 90 days
Primary: change in new developer sign-up conversion within 14 days
Secondary: number of enterprise deals requiring amendment to metering language
Secondary: percent of requests that fall into grace-credit window vs billed floor
Operational: any increase in billing disputes and security questionnaire escalations
rollout_plan: 1) Metric modelling and synthetic workload sims (ENG + PM) — 2 weeks
2) Instrumentation: tag ingress/egress token counts + streaming session IDs (ENG) — feature branch + telemetry PR
3) Billing-sandbox implementation and reconciliation checks (GT) — validate simulated invoices
4) Legal & Security: draft contract clause and SQ talking points; run with 2 pilot EA customers
5) Small beta: 5% of new accounts + opt-in for existing customers for 4 weeks
6) Analysis window + decision: iterate or rollback
acceptance_criteria: A1: Billing sandbox reports match production reconciliation within 0.5% for test workloads
A2: No more than a 5% decrease in 14-day developer conversion for beta cohort
A3: Legal approves contract language and security team signs off on updated SQ answers
A4: Billing disputes remain under baseline (<=2% of pilot invoices)
A5: Observability shows no adverse latency or quota regressions due to metering hooks
